01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 471

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 471
Sūrat al-Ḥadīd is Medinan and has twenty-nine verses [revealed after al-Zalzala]. In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
سورة الحديد مدنية، وهي تسع وعشرون آية [نزلت بعد الزلزلة] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 57:1–6 · Vol. 4, pp. 471–473

Verses 1 to 6

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God, and He is the Almighty, the Wise (1). His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things (2). He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things (3). It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself on the Throne. He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends in it. He is with you wherever you are, and God sees what you do (4). His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to God all matters are returned (5). He causes the night to enter into the day and the day to enter into the night, and He is Knowing of what is in the breasts (6)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (1) لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (2) هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْباطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ (3) هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما يَخْرُجُ مِنْها وَما يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَما يَعْرُجُ فِيها وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (4) لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ (5) يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ (6)
Vol. 4, p. 471
.
Vol. 4, p. 472
In some of the opening verses sabbaḥa comes in the past form, and in some in the present form, and each of them means that it is in the nature of the one to whom glorification is attributed to glorify Him; that is his constant habit and custom. This verb is made transitive by the lām at one time and by itself at another, as in the saying of the Exalted “and glorify Him” (tusabbiḥūhu). Its original is to be transitive by itself, because the meaning of sabbaḥtuhu is “I distanced Him from evil,” transferred from sabaḥa when one goes away and is distant. The lām must be either like the lām in naṣaḥtuhu and naṣaḥtu lahu, or sabbaḥa li-llāh is meant as: he produced glorification for the sake of God and His countenance sincerely. “Whatever is in the heavens and the earth”: whatever is capable of glorification and for which it is valid. If you ask: What is the syntactic place of yuḥyī? I answer: it is possible that it has no place and is a sentence on its own, like “His is the dominion of the heavens”; or that it is in the nominative, as in “[He] gives life and causes death”; or in the accusative as a circumstantial from the pronoun in “lahu,” with the prepositional phrase governing it. Its meaning is: He gives life to sperm and eggs and to the dead on the Day of Resurrection, and causes the living to die. “He is the First” means the Ancient, who was before everything; “and the Last,” who remains after the destruction of everything; “and the Manifest,” through the proofs that point to Him; “and the Hidden,” because He is not perceived by the senses. If you ask: What is the meaning of the conjunctions? «1» I answer: the first wāw indicates «2» that He combines the two attributes of priority and posteriority, and the third that He combines manifestness and concealment. As for the middle one, it indicates that He combines the totality of the first two attributes and the totality of the last two. So He is continuously existent in all the past and coming times, and in all of them He is manifest and hidden, combining manifestness through proofs and concealment, so that He is not perceived by the senses. In this there is an argument against whoever permits His being perceived «3» in the Hereafter by the sense. It is also said that “the Manifest” is the one above everything and prevailing over it, from ẓahara ʿalayhi when one surmounted and overcame it; and “the Hidden” is the one who knew the inside of everything (baṭana kull shayʾ), that is, its inner reality; but that is not so, because it departs from the understood apparent sense.
جاء في بعض الفواتح سَبَّحَ على لفظ الماضي، وفي بعضها على لفظ المضارع، وكل واحد منهما معناه: أنّ من شأن من أسند إليه التسبيح أن يسبحه، وذلك هجيراه وديدنه، وقد عدى هذا الفعل باللام تارة وبنفسه أخرى في قوله تعالى وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ وأصله: التعدي بنفسه، لأنّ معنى سبحته: بعدته عن السوء، منقول من سبح إذا ذهب وبعد، فاللام لا تخلو إما أن تكون مثل اللام في: نصحته، ونصحت له. وإما أن يراد بسبح لله: أحدث التسبيح لأجل الله ولوجهه خالصا، ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ما يتأتى منه التسبيح ويصح. فإن قلت: ما محل يُحْيِي؟ قلت: يجوز أن لا يكون له محل، ويكون جملة برأسها، كقوله لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وأن يكون مرفوعا على: هو يحيى ويميت، ومنصوبا حالا من المجرور في لَهُ والجار عاملا فيها. ومعناه: يحيى النطف والبيض والموتى يوم القيامة ويميت الأحياء هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ هو القديم الذي كان قبل كل شيء وَالْآخِرُ الذي يبقى بعد هلاك كل شيء وَالظَّاهِرُ بالأدلة الدالة عليه وَالْباطِنُ لكونه غير مدرك بالحواس. فإن قلت: فما معنى الواو؟ «1» قلت الواو الأولى معناها الدلالة «2» على أنه الجامع بين الصفتين الأولية والآخرية، والثالثة على أنه الجامع بين الظهور والخفاء. وأما الوسطى، فعلى أنه الجامع بين مجموع الصفتين الأوليين ومجموع الصفتين الأخريين، فهو المستمر الوجود في جميع الأوقات الماضية والآتية، وهو في جميعها ظاهر وباطن: جامع للظهور بالأدلة والخفاء، فلا يدرك بالحواس. وفي هذا حجة على من جوّز إدراكه «3» في الآخرة بالحاسة. وقيل: الظاهر العالي على كل شيء الغالب له، من ظهر عليه إذا علاه وغلبه. والباطن الذي بطن كل شيء، أى علم باطنه، وليس بذاك مع العدول عن الظاهر المفهوم.
Vol. 4, p. 473
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 472
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “If you ask: What is the meaning of the wāw? And he answered that the middle one between the First and the Last is for combining the meaning of priority and remaining … etc. He said: the meaning of the Manifest is by proofs, and of the Hidden is from the senses. It is also said: in it is evidence refuting those who claim that He the Exalted will be seen in the Hereafter by the sense.” Aḥmad said: There is no evidence in it for that. We may say that what is meant is the absence of perception by the sense in this world and not in the Hereafter, and we say so; or in the Hereafter, with the intended being the unbelievers and those who deny the vision, such as the Qadariyya. Do you not see His words “No indeed; on that day they will be veiled from their Lord”? If it is said that this is a restriction and specification contrary to the apparent sense, we say: the question is a definitive one, so a possibility suffices. Also, its counterpart necessarily has a specification, because God the Exalted did not make all His creatures manifest through the proofs that lead to knowing Him; rather He hid them from many of them and deprived them of the success of believing in Him, mighty and majestic. So the apparent sense of “the Manifest” is, in specification, like the second [“the Hidden”], in conformity between it and the first.
2. . His statement «qultu al-wāw al-ūlā maʿnāhā al-dalāla»: the first indicates only the combination of the first two attributes, the third the combination of the nearer two, and the second the combination of the two sets. (ʿ)
3. . His statement «ḥujja ʿalā man jawwaza idrākahu»: he means the Sunnīs. They permitted seeing Him absolutely and said “Eyes do not comprehend Him,” that is, they do not encompass Him, while the Muʿtazila held His being seen to be impossible; the details are in the discussion of tawḥīd. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إن قلت: ما معنى الواو وأجاب بأن المتوسطة بين الأول والآخر للجمع بين معنى الأولية والبقاء الخ. قال: ومعنى الطاهر أى بالأدلة والباطن أى عن الحواس. وقيل: وفيه دليل الرد على من زعم أنه تعالى يرى في الآخرة بالحاسة» قال أحمد: «لا دليل فيه على ذلك، فان لنا أن نقول: إن المراد عدم الإدراك بالحاسة في الدنيا لا في الآخرة. ونحن نقول به، أو في الآخرة. والمراد: الكفار والجاحدون للرؤية كالقدرية ألا ترى إلى قوله كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ فانه قيل: تقييد وتخصيص على خلاف الظاهر. قلنا والمسألة قطعية، فيكفى الاحتمال. وأيضا فقسيمه لا بد فيه من تخصيص، فانه تعالى لم يظهر جميع خلقه على الأدلة الموصلة إلى معرفته، بل أخفاها عن كثير منهم وحرمهم الفوز بالايمان به عز وجل، فالظاهر إذا معناها في التخصيص كالثاني طبقا بينه وبين الأول.
2. . قوله «قلت الواو الأولى معناها الدلالة» الأولى إنما دلت على اجتماع الصفتين الأوليين، والثالثة على اجتماع الأقربين. والثانية على اجتماع المجموعين. (ع)
3. . قوله «حجة على من جوز إدراكه» يريد أهل السنة، وهم قد جوزوا رؤيته مطلقا، وقالوا: لا تدركه الأبصار، أى لا تحيط به، والمعتزلة أحالوا رؤيته تعالى، وتفصيله في التوحيد. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 473
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “Taking the covenant is an expression for constructing intellects in them … etc.” Aḥmad said: What prevents him from taking the taking of the covenant as what God made clear in a verse other than this, when the Exalted says: “And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify against themselves: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes’”? What makes me doubtful about him is his denial of many such apparent texts and turning them away from their realities, despite their rational possibility and their definite occurrence in the transmitted texts, toward what he imagines to be a similitude that he calls takhyīl. So the rule on which you should rely, so that what he hints at does not harm you, is that whatever reason permits and the transmitted text reports as occurring must be taken on its apparent sense [the printed wording here reads “mā kull mā”]. And God is the grantor of success.
2. . His statement «wa-quriʾa: akhadha mīthāqakum» shows that the reading in the passive voice is better known. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «أخذ الميثاق عبارة عن تركيب العقول فيهم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وما عليه أن يحمل أخذ الميثاق على ما بينه الله في آية غير هذه، إذ يقول تعالى وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قالُوا بَلى ولقد يريبني منه إنكاره لكثير من مثل هذه الظواهر والعدول بها عن حقائقها مع إمكانها عقلا ووقوعها بالسمع قطعا إلى ما يتوهمه من تمثيل يسميه تخييلا، فالقاعدة التي تعتمد عليها كى لا يضرك ما يومئ إليه أن ما كل ما جوزه العقل وورد بوقوعه السمع وجب حمله على ظاهره والله الموفق.
2. . قوله «وقرئ: أخذ ميثاقكم» يفيد أن القراءة على البناء للمفعول أشهر. (ع)
03
Q 57:7–8 · Vol. 4, p. 473

Verses 7 to 8

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Believe in God and His Messenger, and spend of that in which He has made you successors; those of you who believe and spend will have a great reward (7). What is the matter with you that you do not believe in God, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has taken your covenant, if you are believers (8)
آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَأَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا جَعَلَكُمْ مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَأَنْفَقُوا لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ (7) وَما لَكُمْ لا تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ (8)
Vol. 4, p. 473
? “Successors in it” means that the property in your hands is God's property, by His creating and originating it; He only gave it to you in possession and gave you license to enjoy it and made you vicegerents in disposing of it, so it is not your property in reality. You are in it only in the position of agents and deputies, so spend from it on God's rights, and let spending from it be easy on you, as spending from another's property is easy for a man when he has been given leave in it. Or: He made you successors of those who were before you in what is in your hands, by having it pass to you as inheritance; so take a lesson from their state, in that it passed from them to you and will pass from you to those after you, and do not be stingy with it, but benefit yourselves by spending from it. “Lā tuʾminūna” is a circumstantial clause from the meaning of the verb in “mā lakum,” as you say “mā laka qāʾiman,” in the sense of “what are you doing standing?”, that is: what is the matter with you, disbelieving in God? And the wāw in “wa-l-rasūlu yadʿūkum” is the wāw of circumstance, so they are two nested circumstantial clauses. It is also read “wa-mā lakum lā tuʾminūna bi-llāhi wa-l-rasūlu yadʿūkum.” The meaning is: what excuse do you have for leaving faith when the Messenger calls you to it, alerts you to it, and recites to you the Book that speaks with demonstrations and proofs; and before that God had taken your covenant to believe, since He constructed intellects in you «1», set up proofs for you, enabled you to reflect, and removed your pretexts. So since no pretext remains for you after the proofs of reason and the Messenger's alerting, what is the matter with you that you do not believe, “if you are believers” for some reason that requires it, for this requirement can be exceeded by no other. It is also read “akhadha mīthāqakum” «2» in the active voice, the agent being God, mighty and majestic.
مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ يعنى أن الأموال التي في أيديكم إنما هي أموال الله بخلقه وإنشائه لها، وإنما موّلكم إياها، وخوّلكم الاستمتاع بها، وجعلكم خلفاء في التصرف فيها، فليست هي بأموالكم في الحقيقة. وما أنتم فيها إلا بمنزلة الوكلاء والنوّاب، فأنفقوا منها في حقوق الله، وليهن عليكم الإنفاق منها كما يهون على الرجل النفقة من مال غيره إذا أذن له فيه. أو جعلكم مستخلفين ممن كان قبلكم فيما في أيديكم: بتوريثه إياكم، فاعتبروا بحالهم حيث انتقل منهم إليكم، وسينقل منكم إلى من بعدكم، فلا تبخلوا به، وانفعوا بالإنفاق منها أنفسكم لا تُؤْمِنُونَ حال من معنى الفعل في مالكم، كما تقول: مالك قائما، بمعنى: ما تصنع قائما، أى: وما لكم كافرين بالله. والواو في وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ واو الحال، فهما حالان متداخلتان. وقرئ: وَما لَكُمْ لا تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ والمعنى: وأى عذر لكم في ترك الإيمان والرسول يدعوكم إليه وينبهكم عليه ويتلو عليكم الكتاب الناطق بالبراهين والحجج، وقبل ذلك قد أخذ الله ميثاقكم بالإيمان: حيث ركب فيكم العقول، «1» ونصب لكم الأدلة، ومكنكم من النظر، وأزاح عللكم، فإذ لم تبق لكم علة بعد أدلة العقول وتنبيه الرسول، فما لكم لا تؤمنون إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ لموجب ما، فإن هذا الموجب لا مزيد عليه. وقرئ: أخذ ميثاقكم، «2» على البناء للفاعل، وهو الله عز وجل.

Q 57:9 · Vol. 4, pp. 473–474

Verse 9

The verse as the commentary quotes it
It is He who sends down upon His servant clear signs to bring you out of the darknesses into the light; and God is Compassionate and Merciful to you (9)
هُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ عَلى عَبْدِهِ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُمْ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ (9)
Vol. 4, p. 473
. “To bring you out” means that God brings you out by His signs from the darknesses of unbelief into the light of faith; or that the Messenger brings you out by his call
لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ الله بآياته من ظلمات الكفر إلى نور الإيمان. أو ليخرجكم الرسول بدعوته
Vol. 4, p. 474
“La-raʾūf” is also read la-ruʾūf «1».
لَرَؤُفٌ وقرئ لرؤوف «1» .
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 473
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “Taking the covenant is an expression for constructing intellects in them … etc.” Aḥmad said: What prevents him from taking the taking of the covenant as what God made clear in a verse other than this, when the Exalted says: “And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify against themselves: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes’”? What makes me doubtful about him is his denial of many such apparent texts and turning them away from their realities, despite their rational possibility and their definite occurrence in the transmitted texts, toward what he imagines to be a similitude that he calls takhyīl. So the rule on which you should rely, so that what he hints at does not harm you, is that whatever reason permits and the transmitted text reports as occurring must be taken on its apparent sense [the printed wording here reads “mā kull mā”]. And God is the grantor of success.
2. . His statement «wa-quriʾa: akhadha mīthāqakum» shows that the reading in the passive voice is better known. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «أخذ الميثاق عبارة عن تركيب العقول فيهم
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وما عليه أن يحمل أخذ الميثاق على ما بينه الله في آية غير هذه، إذ يقول تعالى وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قالُوا بَلى ولقد يريبني منه إنكاره لكثير من مثل هذه الظواهر والعدول بها عن حقائقها مع إمكانها عقلا ووقوعها بالسمع قطعا إلى ما يتوهمه من تمثيل يسميه تخييلا، فالقاعدة التي تعتمد عليها كى لا يضرك ما يومئ إليه أن ما كل ما جوزه العقل وورد بوقوعه السمع وجب حمله على ظاهره والله الموفق.
2. . قوله «وقرئ: أخذ ميثاقكم» يفيد أن القراءة على البناء للمفعول أشهر. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 474
1. (1) . His statement «and it is read la-ruʾūf» shows that the short reading is better known, but that is open to question, so it should be examined. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: ruʾifa bihi (with ḍamma), raʾafa bihi (with fatḥa), and raʾifa bihi (with kasra); so he is raʾūf, on the pattern faʿūl. Kaʿb b. Mālik al-Anṣārī said: “We obey our Prophet and obey a Lord … He is the Merciful, who was compassionate (raʾūfan) toward us.” And also raʾuf, on the pattern faʿul. Jarīr said: “He sees that the Muslims have a right upon him … like the act of the compassionate, merciful father.” The apparent point is that its spelling is with one wāw in both the long and the short readings, so the better-known reading would be the long one, as it is better known in linguistic usage. (ʿ)
2. . Agreed upon, from the hadith of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī ؓ. [.....]
3. . His statement «wa-quriʾā manṣūbayn ʿalā jawāb»: that is, His words fa-yuḍāʿifahu and fa-yuḍʿifahu. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله وقرئ «لرؤوف» يفيد أن القراءة بالقصر أشهر، وفيه نظر فلينظر. وفي الصحاح: رؤف به- بالضم، ورأف به- بالفتح، ورئف به- بالكسر، فهو رؤف على فعول. قال كعب بن مالك الأنصارى: نطيع نبينا ونطيع ربا
…. هو الرحمن كان بنا رءوفا ورؤف أيضا على فعل. قال جرير: يرى للمسلمين عليه حقا
…. كفعل الوالد الرؤوف الرحيم والظاهر أن رسمه بواو واحدة حال المد والقصر، فيكون الأشهر قراءة المد، كما هو الأشهر في الاستعمال اللغوي. (ع)
2. . متفق عليه من حديث أبى سعيد الخدرى رضى الله عنه. [.....]
3. . قوله «وقرئا منصوبين على جواب» أى قوله: فيضاعفه، وقوله فيضعفه. (ع)
05
Q 57:10–11 · Vol. 4, pp. 474–475

Verses 10 to 11

The verses as the commentary quotes them
What is the matter with you that you do not spend in the way of God, when to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought; those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought; and to each God has promised the best; and God is aware of what you do (10). Who is it that will lend God a good loan, that He may multiply it for him, and for him is a generous reward (11)
وَما لَكُمْ أَلاَّ تُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لا يَسْتَوِي مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْفَتْحِ وَقاتَلَ أُولئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَقاتَلُوا وَكُلاًّ وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (10) مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ وَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ (11)
Vol. 4, p. 474
? “What is the matter with you that you do not spend” means: that you not spend. “And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth”: He inherits everything in them, and nothing of it remains for anyone, of property or otherwise. He means: what purpose do you have in leaving spending in the way of God and jihād with His Messenger, when God will destroy you and so inherit your property? This is among the most emphatic incitements to spending in the way of God. Then He made clear the difference among those of them who spend, and said “Not equal among you are those who spent” before the conquest of Mecca, before the might of Islam and the strength of its people and people's entering the religion of God in throngs, and when there was little need of fighting and spending on it, “and those who spent after the conquest,” which is omitted because the indication is clear. “Those” who spent before the conquest, who are the foremost and first of the Emigrants and Anṣār, about whom the Prophet ﷺ said: “If one of you spent the like of Uḥud in gold, it would not reach a mudd of one of them, nor half of it” «2», “are greater in rank.” It is also read qabla l-fatḥi. “And to each,” that is, each one of the two groups, “God has promised the best,” that is, the best reward, which is Paradise, with differences of degrees. It is also read in the nominative: wa-kullun waʿadahu llāh. It is said that it was revealed regarding Abū Bakr ؓ because he was the first to accept Islam and the first to spend in the way of God. The good loan is spending in His way. He likened that to a loan by way of metaphor, because when one gives his property for His sake, it is as if he lent it to Him; “that He may multiply it for him” means He gives him his reward for his spending multiplied, manifold, from His bounty; “and for him is a generous reward” means: that reward, with the multiples added to it, is generous in itself. It is also read fa-yuḍaʿʿifahu. Both are read in the accusative as an answer «3» to the question, and the nominative by conjunction to yuqriḍu or to fa-yuḍāʿifahu.
وَما لَكُمْ أَلَّا تُنْفِقُوا في أن لا تنفقوا وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يرث كل شيء فيهما لا يبقى منه باق لأحد من مال وغيره، يعنى: وأى غرض لكم في ترك الإنفاق في سبيل الله والجهاد مع رسوله والله مهلككم فوارث أموالكم، وهو من أبلغ البعث على الإنفاق في سبيل الله. ثم بين التفاوت بين المنفقين منهم فقال لا يَسْتَوِي مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ قبل فتح مكة قبل عز الإسلام وقوّة أهله ودخول الناس في دين الله أفواجا وقلة الحاجة إلى القتال والنفقة فيه، ومن أنفق من بعد الفتح فحذف لوضوح الدلالة أُولئِكَ الذين أنفقوا قبل الفتح وهم السابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار الذين قال فيهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لو أنفق أحدكم مثل أحد ذهبا ما بلغ مدّ أحدهم ولا نصيفه» «2» أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً. وقرئ: قبل الفتح وَكُلًّا وكل واحد من الفريقين وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى أى المثوبة الحسنى وهي الجنة مع تفاوت الدرجات. وقرئ بالرفع على: وكل وعده الله. وقيل: نزلت في أبى بكر رضى الله عنه، لأنه أول من أسلم وأول من أنفق في سبيل الله. القرض الحسن: الإنفاق في سبيله. شبه ذلك بالقرض على سبيل المجاز، لأنه إذا أعطى ماله لوجهه فكأنه أقرضه إياه فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ أى يعطيه أجره على إنفاقه مضاعفا «أضعافا» من فضله وَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ يعنى: وذلك الأجر المضموم إليه الأضعاف كريم في نفسه. وقرئ: فيضعفه. وقرئا منصوبين على جواب «3» الاستفهام «والرفع عطف على يُقْرِضُ، أو على فَيُضاعِفَهُ.
Vol. 4, p. 475

06
Q 57:12 · Vol. 4, p. 475

Verse 12

The verse as the commentary quotes it
On the day you see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right: “Your good tidings today are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein.” That is the great triumph (12)
يَوْمَ تَرَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ يَسْعى نُورُهُمْ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ بُشْراكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ (12)
Vol. 4, p. 475
. “Yawma tarā” is a temporal adverb for His words “and for him is a generous reward,” or is accusative by an implied “remember,” in magnification of that day. He said “before them and on their right” only because the blessed are given the records of their deeds from these two directions, just as the wretched are given them from their left and from behind their backs. So He made the light in the two directions their badge and sign, because they are those who were made blessed by their good deeds and prospered by their white records. So when they are taken to Paradise and pass over the Bridge, running, that light runs with their running at their side and ahead of them. And those of the angels who receive them say to them: “Your good tidings today.” It is also read dhālika l-fawz.
يَوْمَ تَرَى ظرف لقوله: وله أجر كريم. أو منصوب بإضمار «اذكر» تعظيما لذلك اليوم. وإنما قال بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ لأنّ السعداء يؤتون صحائف أعمالهم من هاتين الجهتين، كما أن الأشقياء يؤتونها من شمائلهم ومن وراء ظهورهم، فجعل النور في الجهتين شعارا لهم وآية، لأنهم هم الذين بحسناتهم سعدوا وبصحائفهم البيض أفلحوا، فإذا ذهب بهم إلى الجنة ومروا على الصراط يسعون: سعى بسعيهم ذلك النور جنيبا لهم ومتقدما. ويقول لهم الذين يتلقونهم من الملائكة. بُشْراكُمُ الْيَوْمَ. وقرئ: ذلك الفوز.

07
Q 57:13–15 · Vol. 4, pp. 475–476

Verses 13 to 15

The verses as the commentary quotes them
On the day the hypocritical men and hypocritical women say to those who believed: “Wait for us, that we may take some of your light.” It is said: “Go back behind you and seek light.” Then a wall with a gate is set up between them; its inside has mercy, and its outside, facing it, is punishment (13). They call out to them: “Were we not with you?” They say: “Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, waited, doubted, and were deluded by wishes until God's command came, and the deceiver deceived you about God” (14). So today no ransom is accepted from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is your mawlā, and wretched is the destination (15)
يَوْمَ يَقُولُ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالْمُنافِقاتُ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا انْظُرُونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَراءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُوراً فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِسُورٍ لَهُ بابٌ باطِنُهُ فِيهِ الرَّحْمَةُ وَظاهِرُهُ مِنْ قِبَلِهِ الْعَذابُ (13) يُنادُونَهُمْ أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ قالُوا بَلى وَلكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ وَارْتَبْتُمْ وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمانِيُّ حَتَّى جاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ (14) فَالْيَوْمَ لا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ وَلا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ هِيَ مَوْلاكُمْ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ (15)
Vol. 4, p. 475
. “Yawma yaqūlu” is a substitute for “yawma tarā.” “Unẓurūnā” means “wait for us,” because the believers are hurried to Paradise like flashing lightning, on mounts that are driven «1» swiftly with them, while these are on foot. Or it means “look at us,” because when they look at them they face them with their faces while the light is before them, so they are illuminated by it. It is also read anẓirūnā, from naẓira, which means a delay: He made their slowness in going, until they catch up with them, a granting of respite to them. “That we may take some of your light” is accusative from it, which is that they catch up with them and seek light from it. “It is said: go back behind you and seek light” is a rebuff to them and a mockery of them, that is: go back to the standing place, to where this light was given to us, and seek it there, for from there it is taken. Or: go back to the world and seek light by acquiring its cause, which is faith. Or: go back disappointed and stand aside from us,
يَوْمَ يَقُولُ بدل من يوم ترى انْظُرُونا انتظرونا، لأنهم يسرع بهم إلى الجنة كالبروق الخاطفة على ركاب تزف «1» بهم. وهؤلاء مشاة. وانظروا إلينا، لأنهم إذا نظروا اليهم استقبلوهم بوجوههم والنور بين أيديهم فيستضيئون به. وقرئ: أنظرونا من النظرة وهي الإمهال: جعل اتئادهم في المضي إلى أن يلحقوا بهم إنظارا لهم نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ نصب منه، وذلك أن يلحقوا بهم فيستنيروا به قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَراءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُوراً طرد لهم وتهكم بهم، أى: ارجعوا إلى الموقف إلى حيث أعطينا هذا النور فالتمسوه هنالك، فمن ثم يقتبس. أو ارجعوا إلى الدنيا، فالتمسوا نورا بتحصيل سببه وهو الإيمان. أو ارجعوا خائبين وتنحوا عنا،
Vol. 4, p. 476
so seek another light, for there is no way for you to this light.” They knew that there was no light behind them; it is only a disappointment and a dashing of their hopes. “So a wall was set up between them” — between the believers and the hypocrites — a barrier standing between the side of Paradise and the side of the Fire. It is also said: it is al-Aʿrāf. “That wall has a gate” for the people of Paradise to enter by; “its inside” is the inner side of the wall or of the gate, which is the side toward Paradise; “and its outside” is what appears to the people of the Fire; “from before it,” that is, from beside it and from its direction, “is the punishment,” which is the darkness and the fire. Zayd b. ʿAlī ؓ read fa-ḍaraba baynahum in the active voice. “Were we not with you?” They mean their agreement with them outwardly. “You led yourselves into temptation”: you tried them with hypocrisy and destroyed them; “and you waited” for misfortunes to befall the believers; “and wishes deluded you,” that is, length of hopes and greed for long lives, “until God's command came,” which is death; “and the deceiver deceived you about God,” that is, Satan deceived you by saying that God is Forgiving and Generous and will not punish you. It is also read al-ghurūr with ḍamma. “Ransom” is that by which one ransoms oneself. “It is your mawlā”: it is said, it is more fitting for you; and he cited the saying of Labīd: “So she bolted, thinking that both flanks … are the mawlā of fear, behind her and before her” «1». The true sense of “mawlākum” is maḥrākum and maqminakum «2», that is, your place of which it is said “it is the most fitting for you,” just as it is said “it is a mi'na of generosity,” that is, a place, from someone's saying “he is truly generous.” It is also possible that it means: it is your helper, that is, you have no helper other than it. What is meant is the categorical negation of any helper. Similar is their saying: “So-and-so was afflicted with such-and-such, so he sought the help of impatience” «3». And of this is His saying “they will be helped with water like molten brass.” It is also said: it takes charge of you, as you took charge in the world of the deeds of the people of the Fire.
فالتمسوا نورا آخر، فلا سبيل لكم إلى هذا النور، وقد علموا أن لا نور وراءهم، وإنما هو تخييب وإقناط لهم فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِسُورٍ بين المؤمنين والمنافقين بحائط حائل بين شق الجنة وشق النار. وقيل: هو الأعراف لذلك السور بابٌ لأهل الجنة يدخلون منه باطِنُهُ باطن السور أو الباب، وهو الشق الذي بلى الجنة وَظاهِرُهُ ما ظهر لأهل النار مِنْ قِبَلِهِ من عنده ومن جهته الْعَذابُ وهو الظلمة والنار. وقرأ زيد بن على رضى الله عنهما: فضرب بينهم على البناء للفاعل أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ يريدون موافقتهم في الظاهر فَتَنْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ محنتموها بالنفاق وأهلكتموها وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ بالمؤمنين الدوائر وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمانِيُّ طول الآمال والطمع في امتداد الأعمار حَتَّى جاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وهو الموت وَغَرَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ وغرّكم الشيطان بأنّ الله عفوّ كريم لا يعذبكم. وقرئ: الغرور، بالضم فِدْيَةٌ ما يفتدى به هِيَ مَوْلاكُمْ قيل: هي أولى بكم، وأنشد قول لبيد: فندت كلا الفرجين تحسب أنّه … مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها «1» وحقيقة مولاكم: محراكم ومقمنكم «2» . أى: مكانكم الذي يقال فيه هو أولى بكم، كما قيل: هو مئنة للكرم، أى مكان، لقول القائل: إنه لكريم. ويجوز أن يراد: هي ناصركم، أى لا ناصر لكم غيرها. والمراد: نفى الناصر على البتات. ونحوه قولهم: أصيب فلان بكذا فاستنصر الجزع «3» . ومنه قوله تعالى يُغاثُوا بِماءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ وقيل: تتولاكم كما توليتم في الدنيا أعمال أهل النار.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 475
1. (1) . His statement «tazuffu bihim»: that is, hurries. This is stated in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «تزف بهم» أى: تسرع. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 476
1. (1) . And she became wary of the hunter's faint sound, and it startled her
…. from out of sight, and the hunter was her sickness. So she went, thinking both flanks
…. the mawlā of fear, behind her and before her. By Labīd, from his Muʿallaqa. He is describing a wild cow. Tawajjasat means the cow listened closely; tawajjus is listening. It is said razzat al-samāʾ razzan (with the rāʾ put first) when it sounds at rain; razz with fatḥa is a faint sound, and with kasra a name for a faint sound. Razza: that is, the sound of the unʾnīs, who is the hunter, and he startled her from out of sight. The insertion of “back” in a construction like this is an exaggeration of concealment, because what is behind the back is not known and one does not know what it is. The hunter is called anīs relative to us, not to her, because he is her affliction and the cause of her fear, so he made him sickness itself, by way of exaggeration. Kilā l-farjayn is the subject; and taḥsabu annahu mawlā l-makhāfa is the predicate, that is, that it is the most fitting for fear from its direction. Khalfahā wa-amāmahā is a predicate of an omitted subject, or a substitute from kilā l-farjayn for clarification and explanation, that is: for both is what is between her hind legs and what is between her forelegs; some interpret the two as two notches in the mountain, and on that reading the lām of familiarity in them has no meaning.
2. . His statement «maḥrākum wa-maqminakum»: it is said huwa ḥarin an yafʿala kadhā and huwa qaminun an yafʿalahu, that is, fit and worthy of it. Stated in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
3. . His statement «fa-stanṣara l-jazaʿ»: perhaps it is: al-jazaʿ, that is, the opposite of patience. (ʿ)
1. (1) . وتوجست رز الأنيس فراعها
…. عن ظهر غيب والأنيس سقامها فغدت كلا الفرجين تحسب أنه
…. مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها البيد من معلقته. يصف بقرة وحشية، توجست: أى تسمعت البقرة. والتوجس: التسمع. ويقال: رزت السماء رزا، بتقديم الراء إذا صوتت عند المطر فالرز بالفتح: التصويت الخفي، وبالكسر: اسم للصوت الخفي. ورز: أى صوت الأنيس، وهم الصياد، فأفزعها بظهر الغيب. وإقحام الظهر في مثل هذا التركيب: مبالغة في الخفاء، لأن ما وراء الظهر لا يعلم ولا يدرى ما هو. وسمى الصياد أنيسا بالنسبة إلينا لا إليها، لأنه عناؤها وسبب خوفها، فجعله نفس السقام مبالغة. وكلا الفرحين: مبتدأ. وتحسب أنه مولى المخافة: خبر، أى أنه الأولى بالخوف من جهته. وخلفها وأمامها: خبر لمبتدإ محذوف، أو بدل من كلا الفرجين للتوضيح والتبيين، أى: لهما ما بين رجليها وما بين يديها، وبعضهم فسرهما بنقرنين في الجبل، وعليه فلا معنى للام العهد فيهما.
2. . قوله «محراكم ومقمنكم» يقال: هو حرى أن يفعل كذا، وهو قمن أن يفعله، أى: جدير بذلك وحقيق به. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
3. . قوله «فاستنصر الجزع» لعله: الجزع، أى: نقيض الصبر. (ع)

Q 57:16 · Vol. 4, pp. 476–477

Verse 16

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves at the remembrance of God and what has come down of the truth, and that they not be like those who were given the Book before, for whom the term grew long so their hearts hardened, and many of them are defiantly disobedient (16)
أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَما نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ وَلا يَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَطالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَمَدُ فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ (16)
Vol. 4, p. 477
“Has the time not come” (a-lam yaʾni) is from anā l-amru yaʾnī, when its ināh came, that is, its time. It is also read a-lam yaʾin, from āna yaʾīnu, with the meaning of anā yaʾnī, and a-lammā yaʾni. It is said that they were in drought in Mecca, and when they emigrated they received provision and comfort and slackened from what they had been upon, so this was revealed. From Ibn Masʿūd: “There were only four years between our becoming Muslim and our being reproached with this verse” «1». From Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both: God found the hearts of the believers slow and reproached them at the head of thirteen years from the revelation of the Qurʾān. From al-Ḥasan ؓ: By God, He found them slow while they recited of the Qurʾān less than you recite; so consider the length of what you have recited of it and the iniquity that has appeared among you. From Abū Bakr ؓ: this verse was recited in his presence while some people of al-Yamāma were with him, and they wept intensely; he looked at them and said: “So we were, until the hearts hardened.” It is also read nazzala and nazala, and anzala. “And not be” is conjoined to takhshaʿa; it is also read with tāʾ as a shift of address. It may also be a prohibition to them against resembling the People of the Book in hardness of heart after they had been rebuked: that is because the truth used to stand between the Children of Israel and their desires, and when they heard the Torah and the Gospel they humbled themselves to God and their hearts softened; then when time grew long upon them, coarseness and hardness overcame them, they differed, and introduced what they introduced of distortion and otherwise.
أَلَمْ يَأْنِ من أنى الأمر يأنى، إذا جاء إناه، أى. وقته. وقرئ: ألم يئن، من آن يئين بمعنى: أنى يأنى، وألما يأن، قيل: كانوا مجدبين بمكة، فلما هاجروا أصابوا الرزق والنعمة ففتروا عما كانوا عليه، فنزلت. وعن ابن مسعود: ما كان بين إسلامنا وبين أن عوتبنا بهذه الآية إلا أربع سنين «1» . وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: أنّ الله استبطأ قلوب المؤمنين فعاتبهم على رأس ثلاث عشرة من نزول القرآن. وعن الحسن رضى الله عنه: أما والله لقد استبطأهم وهم يقرؤن من القرآن أقل مما تقرءون. فانظروا في طول ما قرأتم منه وما ظهر فيكم من الفسق. وعن أبى بكر رضى الله عنه أنّ هذه الآية قرئت بين يديه وعنده قوم من أهل اليمامة، فبكوا بكاء شديدا، فنظر إليهم فقال: هكذا كنا حتى قست القلوب. وقرئ: نزّل ونزل. وأنزل وَلا يَكُونُوا عطف على تخشع، وقرئ بالتاء على الالتفات. ويجوز أن يكون نهيا لهم عن مماثلة أهل الكتاب في قسوة القلوب بعد أن وبخوا، وذلك أنّ بنى إسرائيل كان الحق يحول بينهم وبين شهواتهم، وإذا سمعوا التوراة والإنجيل خشعوا لله ورقت قلوبهم، فلما طال عليهم الزمان غلبهم الجفاء والقسوة واختلفوا وأحدثوا ما أحدثوا من التحريف وغيره.
Question
If you ask: What is the meaning of “at the remembrance of God and what has come down of the truth”?
فإن قلت: ما معنى لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَما نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ؟
Answer
I answer: it is possible that by the remembrance and by what came down of the truth the Qurʾān is meant, because it combines the two: remembrance and exhortation, and that it is truth descending from heaven; and it is possible that what is meant is the humbling of hearts when God is mentioned and when the Qurʾān is recited, as in His saying “when God is mentioned their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them they increase them in faith.” By “al-amad” He meant the term (ajal), as in the saying: “…… when its term has ended” «2». It is also read al-amadd, that is, the longer time. “And many of them are defiantly disobedient”: going out from their religion, rejecting what is in the two Books.
قلت: يجوز أن يراد بالذكر وبما نزل من الحق: القرآن، لأنه جامع للأمرين: للذكر والموعظة، وأنه حق نازل من السماء، وأن يراد خشوعها إذا ذكر الله وإذا تلى القرآن كقوله تعالى إِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِذا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُهُ زادَتْهُمْ إِيماناً أراد بالأمد: الأجل، كقوله: ...... إذا انتهى أمده «2» وقرئ: الأمدّ، أى: الوقت الأطول وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ خارجون عن دينهم رافضون لما في الكتابين.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 476
1. (1) . And she became wary of the hunter's faint sound, and it startled her
…. from out of sight, and the hunter was her sickness. So she went, thinking both flanks
…. the mawlā of fear, behind her and before her. By Labīd, from his Muʿallaqa. He is describing a wild cow. Tawajjasat means the cow listened closely; tawajjus is listening. It is said razzat al-samāʾ razzan (with the rāʾ put first) when it sounds at rain; razz with fatḥa is a faint sound, and with kasra a name for a faint sound. Razza: that is, the sound of the unʾnīs, who is the hunter, and he startled her from out of sight. 3. . His statement «fa-stanṣara l-jazaʿ»: perhaps it is: al-jazaʿ, that is, the opposite of patience. (ʿ)

Q 57:17 · Vol. 4, pp. 477–478

Verse 17

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. We have made clear the signs for you so that you may understand (17)
اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآياتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (17)
Vol. 4, p. 478
“Know that God gives life to the earth after its death”: it is said this is a likeness of the effect of remembrance in hearts, and that it gives them life as rain gives life to the earth.
اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها قيل: هذا تمثيل لأثر الذكر في القلوب، وأنه يحييها كما يحيى الغيث الأرض.

Q 57:18 · Vol. 4, p. 478

Verse 18

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Indeed the men who give charity and the women who give charity, and have lent God a good loan, it will be multiplied for them, and for them is a generous reward (18)
إِنَّ الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَالْمُصَّدِّقاتِ وَأَقْرَضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً يُضاعَفُ لَهُمْ وَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ (18)
Vol. 4, p. 478
. “Al-muṣṣaddiqīn” means the almsgivers (al-mutaṣaddiqīn). It is also read in the original form. And al-muṣaddiqīn is from ṣaddaqa: those who believed God and His Messenger, that is, the believers.
الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ المتصدّقين. وقرئ على الأصل. والمصدّقين من صدق، وهم الذين صدقوا الله ورسوله يعنى المؤمنين.
Question
If you ask: To what is “and have lent” conjoined?
فإن قلت: علام عطف قوله وَأَقْرَضُوا؟
Answer
I answer: to the meaning of the verb in “al-muṣṣaddiqīn,” because the lām means “those who,” and the active participle has the meaning of “they gave charity,” as if it were said: Indeed those who gave charity and lent. The good loan is to give charity from what is good, with a willing soul and sound intention, to whoever deserves charity. It is also read yuḍʿaf and yuḍāʿaf, with kasra on the ʿayn, that is, God multiplies.
قلت: على معنى الفعل في المصدّقين، لأنّ اللام بمعنى الذين، واسم الفاعل بمعنى اصدقوا، كأنه قيل: إنّ الذين اصدقوا وأقرضوا. والقرض الحسن: أنّ يتصدق من الطيب عن طيبة النفس وصحة النية على المستحق للصدقة. وقرئ: يضعف، ويضاعف، بكسر العين، أى: يضاعف الله.

Vol. 4, p. 478

Q 57:19 · Vol. 4, p. 478

Verse 19

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And those who believe in God and His messengers, those are the truthful and the witnesses before their Lord; they will have their reward and their light. And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Blaze (19)
وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الصِّدِّيقُونَ وَالشُّهَداءُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ (19)
Vol. 4, p. 478
. He means that the believers in God and His messengers are with God in the position of the ṣiddīqūn and the martyrs: they who were first to believe and were martyred in the way of God. “They will have their reward and their light,” that is, like the reward of the ṣiddīqūn and the martyrs and like their light.
يريد أنّ المؤمنين بالله ورسله هم عند الله بمنزلة الصديقين والشهداء: وهم الذين سبقوا إلى التصديق واستشهدوا في سبيل الله لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ أى: مثل أجر الصديقين والشهداء ومثل نورهم.
Question
If you ask: How are they made equal in reward when there must be a difference?
فإن قلت: كيف يسوّى بينهم في الأجر ولا بدّ من التفاوت؟
Answer
I answer: the meaning is that God gives the believers their reward and multiplies it for them by His bounty, until their reward together with its multiples equals the reward of those. It is also possible that “and the martyrs” is a subject and “for them is their reward” is its predicate.
قلت: المعنى أنّ الله يعطى المؤمنين أجرهم ويضاعفه لهم بفضله، حتى يساوى أجرهم مع أضعافه أجر أولئك. ويجوز أن يكون وَالشُّهَداءُ مبتدأ، ولَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ خيره.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 478
1. (1) . His statement «fa-stawā wa-ktahala»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: iktahala l-nabāt, that is, its height was complete and its blossom appeared. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «فاستوى واكتهل» في الصحاح: اكتهل النيات، أى: تم طوله وظهر نوره. (ع)
12
Q 57:20 · Vol. 4, pp. 478–479

Verse 20

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you, and rivalry in wealth and children — like the likeness of a rain whose growth pleases the unbelievers; then it dries and you see it yellowed, then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval; and the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion (20)
اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوالِ وَالْأَوْلادِ كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَباتُهُ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَراهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطاماً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٌ وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلاَّ مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ (20)
Vol. 4, p. 478
. He meant that the world is nothing but trivial matters, which are play, amusement, adornment, boasting and rivalry in increase; while the Hereafter is nothing but great matters, which are severe punishment, forgiveness, and God's approval. He likened the state of the world, the swiftness of its passing along with its little benefit, to a plant that rain made grow, which became upright and matured «1», and pleased
أراد أنّ الدنيا ليست إلا محقرات من الأمور وهي اللعب واللهو والزينة والتفاخر والتكاثر. وأما الآخرة فما هي إلا أمور عظام، وهي: العذاب الشديد والمغفرة ورضوان الله. وشبه حال الدنيا وسرعة تقضيها مع قلة جدواها بنبات أنبته الغيث فاستوى واكتهل «1» وأعجب به
Vol. 4, p. 479
the unbelievers, those who deny God's favor in what He provided them of rain and plants; then He sent a blight upon it, so it dried and yellowed and became debris, as a punishment for them for their denial, as He did to the owners of the garden and the owner of the two gardens. It is also said that “al-kuffār” are the farmers. It is also read muṣfārran.
الكفار الجاحدون لنعمة الله فيما رزقهم من الغيث والنبات، فبعث عليه العاهة فهاج واصفرّ وصار حطاما عقوبة لهم على جحودهم، كما فعل بأصحاب الجنة وصاحب الجنتين. وقيل الْكُفَّارَ: الزراع. وقرئ: مصفارا
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 478
1. (1) . His statement «fa-stawā wa-ktahala»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: iktahala l-nabāt, that is, its height was complete and its blossom appeared. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «فاستوى واكتهل» في الصحاح: اكتهل النيات، أى: تم طوله وظهر نوره. (ع)

Q 57:21 · Vol. 4, p. 479

Verse 21

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose breadth is like the breadth of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers. That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty (21)
سابِقُوا إِلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُها كَعَرْضِ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ أُعِدَّتْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ (21)
Vol. 4, p. 479
. “Sābiqū” means hasten as racers hasten against their peers on the racecourse, to a garden “whose breadth is like the breadth of the heaven and the earth.” Al-Suddī said: like the breadth of the seven heavens and the seven earths. He mentioned breadth rather than length because whatever has breadth and length, its breadth is less than its length, so when its breadth is described as vast, it is known that its length is vaster and more extended. It is also possible that “breadth” means vastness, as in His saying “then he is of broad supplication.” When He belittled the world and made its matter small and magnified the matter of the Hereafter, He urged His servants to hasten to obtain what He promised of that: forgiveness that saves from severe punishment and the triumph of entering Paradise. “That,” the promised forgiveness and Garden, “is God's bounty,” His gift; “He gives it to whom He wills,” and they are the believers.
سابِقُوا سارعوا مسارعة المسابقين لأقرانهم في المضمار، إلى جنة عَرْضُها كَعَرْضِ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ قال السدى: كعرض سبع السماوات وسبع الأرضين، وذكر العرض دون الطول، لأنّ كل ماله عرض وطول فإنّ عرضه أقل من طوله، فإذا وصف عرضه بالبسطة: عرف أنّ طوله أبسط وأمدّ. ويجوز أن يراد بالعرض: البسطة، كقوله تعالى فَذُو دُعاءٍ عَرِيضٍ لما حقر الدنيا وصغر أمرها وعظم أمر الآخرة: بعث عباده على المسارعة إلى نيل ما وعد من ذلك: وهي المغفرة المنجية من العذاب الشديد والفوز بدخول الجنة ذلِكَ الموعود من المغفرة والجنة فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عطاؤه يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وهم المؤمنون.
14
Q 57:22–24 · Vol. 4, pp. 479–480

Verses 22 to 24

The verses as the commentary quotes them
No calamity strikes in the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a Book before We bring it into being; indeed that is easy for God (22), so that you not grieve over what escapes you nor rejoice over what He has given you; and God does not love any self-deluded boaster (23), those who are stingy and enjoin people to stinginess; and whoever turns away, indeed God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy (24)
ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ إِلاَّ فِي كِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَها إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ (22) لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ وَلا تَفْرَحُوا بِما آتاكُمْ وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ (23) الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ (24)
Vol. 4, p. 479
. “The calamity in the earth” is like drought and blights of crops and fruit; “and in yourselves” like diseases and death; “in a Book,” in the Tablet; “before We bring it into being,” meaning the selves or the calamities; “Indeed that,” that is, the decreeing of that and its inscription in a Book, “is easy for God,” though it is hard for servants. Then He gave the reason for that and made clear the wisdom in it, saying “so that you not grieve … nor rejoice,” meaning that when you know that everything is decreed and written with God, your grief over what is lost and your joy over what comes lessen, because one who knows that what he has is certainly bound to be will not have his anguish swell at losing it, since he has accustomed himself to that; likewise one who knows that some good will reach him, and that its reaching him will not pass him by in any case, will not greatly rejoice on obtaining it. “And God does not love any self-deluded
المصيبة في الأرض: نحو الجدب وآفات الزروع والثمار. وفي الأنفس: نحو الأدواء والموت فِي كِتابٍ في اللوح مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَها يعنى الأنفس أو المصائب إِنَّ ذلِكَ إنّ تقدير ذلك وإثباته في كتاب عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ وإن كان عسيرا على العباد، ثم علل ذلك وبين الحكمة فيه فقال لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا … وَلا تَفْرَحُوا يعنى أنكم إذا علمتم أنّ كل شيء مقدر مكتوب عند الله قلّ أساكم على الفائت وفرحكم على الآتي، لأنّ من علم أن ما عنده معقود لا محالة: لم يتفاقم جزعه عند فقده، لأنه وطن نفسه على ذلك، وكذلك من علم أنّ بعض الخير واصل إليه، وأن وصوله لا يفوته بحال: لم يعظم فرحه عند نيله وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ
Vol. 4, p. 480
boaster,” because whoever rejoices in a share of the world and magnifies himself becomes arrogant and boasts of it and is haughty toward people. It is read bi-mā ātākum and atākum, from īta' and itiyān. And in Ibn Masʿūd's reading: bi-mā ūtītum.
فَخُورٍ لأنّ من فرح بحظ من الدنيا وعظم في نفسه: اختال وافتخر به وتكبر على الناس. قرئ: بما آتاكم. وأتاكم، من الإيتاء والإتيان. وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: بما أوتيتم.
Question
If you ask: But no one can control himself, at a harm that befalls him or a benefit he gains, so as not to grieve or rejoice?
فإن قلت: فلا أحد يملك نفسه- عند مضرة تنزل به، ولا عند منفعة ينالها- أن لا يحزن ولا يفرح.
Answer
I answer: what is meant is grief that carries one to what makes him oblivious of patience and submission to God's command and hope for the reward of the patient, and rejoicing that makes one insolent and distracts from gratitude; but as for grief from which a person is hardly ever free while submitting, and joy in God's favor and regard for it along with gratitude, there is no harm in them. “Those who are stingy” is a substitute for “every self-deluded boaster,” as if He said: He does not love those who are stingy, meaning: those who rejoice with insolent joy when they are given wealth and a share of the world, so out of their love for it and its preciousness to them and its greatness in their eyes they withhold it from God's rights and are stingy with it, and it is not enough for them that they are stingy until they urge people to stinginess, make them desire withholding, and make it attractive to them; and all that is the result of their rejoicing in it and their exultation upon obtaining it. “And whoever turns away” from God's commands and prohibitions and does not desist from what He forbade of grief over what is lost and joy over what comes — God is independent of him. It is also read bi-l-bukhl. Nāfiʿ read: fa-inna llāha l-ghaniyy, and it is so in the codices of the people of Medina and Syria.
قلت: المراد: الحزن المخرج إلى ما يذهل صاحبه عن الصبر والتسليم لأمر الله ورجاء ثواب الصابرين، والفرح المطغى الملهى عن الشكر، فأما الحزن الذي لا يكاد الإنسان يخلو منه مع الاستسلام، والسرور بنعمة الله والاعتداد بها مع الشكر: فلا بأس بهما الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بدل من قوله كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ كأنه قال: لا يحب الذين يبخلون، يريد: الذين يفرحون الفرح المطغى إذا رزقوا مالا وحظا من الدنيا فلحبهم له وعزته عندهم وعظمه في عيونهم: يزوونه عن حقوق الله ويبخلون به، ولا يكفيهم أنهم بخلوا حتى يحملوا الناس على البخل ويرغبوهم في الإمساك ويزينوه لهم، وذلك كله نتيجة فرحهم به وبطرهم عند إصابته وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ عن أوامر الله ونواهيه ولم ينته عما نهى عنه من الأسى على الفائت والفرح بالآتى: فإنّ الله غنى عنه. وقرئ: بالبخل. وقرأ نافع: فإنّ الله الغنى، وهو في مصاحف أهل المدينة والشام كذلك.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 480
1. (1) . His statement «wa-l-mīqaʿa wa-l-miṭraqa … etc.»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-mīqaʿa is the hammer (miṭraqa). Al-mīqaʿa is also the long whetstone. Al-mirr is the rope (ḥabl), and al-misḥāh is like the shovel (mijrafa) except that it is of iron. (ʿ)
2. . Al-Thaʿlabī reported it from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, and in its chain is someone I do not know.
1. (1) . قوله «والميقعة والمطرقة
…. الخ» في الصحاح «الميقعة» : المطرقة. والميقعة- أيضا-: المسن الطويل. والمر: الحبل، والمسحاة كالمجرفة، إلا أنها من حديد. (ع)
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي من حديث ابن عمر، وفي إسناده من لا أعرفه.
15
Q 57:25 · Vol. 4, pp. 480–481

Verse 25

The verse as the commentary quotes it
We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that people may uphold justice; and We sent down iron, in which is great might and benefits for people, and so that God may know who helps Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed God is Strong, Almighty (25)
لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ وَأَنْزَلْنا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْمِيزانَ لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ وَأَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَنافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ وَرُسُلَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ (25)
Vol. 4, p. 480
. “We sent Our messengers” means the angels to the prophets “with clear proofs,” with arguments and miracles; “and We sent down with them the Book,” that is, revelation; “and the Balance”: it is reported that Gabriel ﷺ came down with the scale and gave it to Noah and said: Command your people to weigh with it. “And We sent down iron”: it is said that Adam came down from Paradise with five things of iron with him: the anvil, the tongs, the miqʿa, the hammer «1», and the needle. It is also reported: and with him the mirr and the misḥāh. From the Prophet ﷺ: God the Exalted sent down four blessings from heaven to earth: He sent down iron, fire, water, and salt «2». From al-Ḥasan, “and We sent down iron” means: We created it, as in His saying “and He sent down for you of the cattle”; and that is because His commands, His decrees and His rulings descend from heaven. “In it is great might,” which is fighting with it; “and benefits for people,” in their interests, livelihoods and crafts, for there is no craft
لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا يعنى الملائكة إلى الأنبياء بِالْبَيِّناتِ بالحجج والمعجزات وَأَنْزَلْنا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتابَ أى الوحى وَالْمِيزانَ روى أنّ جبريل عليه السلام نزل بالميزان فدفعه إلى نوح وقال: مر قومك يزنوا به وَأَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ قيل: نزل آدم من الجنة ومعه خمسة أشياء من حديد: السندان، والكلبتان، والميقعة، والمطرقة «1» ، والإبرة. وروى: ومعه المر والمسحاة. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنّ الله تعالى أنزل أربع بركات من السماء إلى الأرض: أنزل الحديد، والنار، والماء، والملح «2» . وعن الحسن وَأَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ: خلقناه، كقوله تعالى وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَنْعامِ وذلك أن أوامره تنزل من السماء وقضاياه وأحكامه فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وهو القتال به وَمَنافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ في مصالحهم ومعايشهم وصنائعهم، فما من صناعة
Vol. 4, p. 481
except that iron is a tool in it, or what is made with iron. “And so that God may know who helps Him and His messengers” by using swords, spears and all weapons in striving against the enemies of the religion “unseen,” while He is unseen by them. Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both, said: they help Him and do not see Him. “Indeed God is Strong, Almighty”: independent, through His power and might, in destroying whom He wishes to destroy, apart from them; He only charged them with jihād so that they might benefit from it and, by complying with the command in it, attain reward.
إلا والحديد آلة فيها، أو ما يعمل بالحديد وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ وَرُسُلَهُ باستعمال السيوف والرماح وسائر السلاح في مجاهدة أعداء الدين بِالْغَيْبِ غائبا عنهم، قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: ينصرونه ولا يبصرونه إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ غنى بقدرته وعزته في إهلاك من يريد هلاكه عنهم، وإنما كلفهم الجهاد لينتفعوا به ويصلوا بامتثال الأمر فيه إلى الثواب.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 480
1. (1) . His statement «wa-l-mīqaʿa wa-l-miṭraqa … etc.»: in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-mīqaʿa is the hammer (miṭraqa). Al-mīqaʿa is also the long whetstone. Al-mirr is the rope (ḥabl), and al-misḥāh is like the shovel (mijrafa) except that it is of iron. (ʿ)
2. . Al-Thaʿlabī reported it from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, and in its chain is someone I do not know.
1. (1) . قوله «والميقعة والمطرقة
…. الخ» في الصحاح «الميقعة» : المطرقة. والميقعة- أيضا-: المسن الطويل. والمر: الحبل، والمسحاة كالمجرفة، إلا أنها من حديد. (ع)
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي من حديث ابن عمر، وفي إسناده من لا أعرفه.
Vol. 4, p. 481
1. (1) . Maḥmūd said: “Al-rahbāniyya is the act attributed to the rahbān … etc.” Aḥmad said: There is a difficulty in it, for attribution to a plural in its form is not accepted by them until it is returned to its singular, unless it is said: since al-ruhbān became a specific group, this name, though a plural, became like a proper name for them, and so it was joined to anṣārī, madāʾinī and aʿrābī.
2. . Maḥmūd said: “And it is accusative by an implied verb … etc.” Aḥmad said: In the parsing of this verse Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī floundered and sided with the party of temptation and the sect of innovation, for he parsed rahbāniyya as accusative by an implied verb which the apparent explains, and he justified the impossibility of conjunction, saying: Do you not see that rahbāniyya cannot be taken as conjoined to “We placed” together with its description by “they innovated it,” because what He the Exalted makes they do not innovate? Al-Zamakhsharī too went to the same blameworthy watering-place, and his accursed devil betrayed him, for when he allowed what Abū ʿAlī prevented, making it conjoined, he excused himself for that by distorting “placing” into “granting success,” fleeing from what Abū ʿAlī fled from: the belief that this is created by God the Exalted, and inclining to polytheism and the belief that what they themselves do God the Exalted does not do and does not create. And what is in this verse suffices as proof, after the definitive proofs and rational demonstrations, for the falsity of what the two believed, for He mentioned the locus of mercy and compassion while knowing that its locus is the heart, so He made His saying “in the hearts of those who followed him” an emphasis of His creating these meanings and a depiction of the meaning of creation by mentioning its locus; and if what was meant were something other than created in their hearts by God the Exalted, as the two claimed, His saying “in the hearts of those who followed him” would have no place, and God refuses that His noble Book contain what has no place. May God inspire us with the proof and take us along the clear path; He is the Patron of success and the Giver of verification.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «الرهبانية: الفعلة المنسوبة للرهبان
…. الخ» قال أحمد: وفيه إشكال، فان النسب إلى الجمع على صيغته غير مقبول عندهم حتى يرد إلى مفرده، إلا أن يقال: إنه لما صار الرهبان طائفة مخصوصة صار هذا الاسم- وإن كان جمعا- كالعلم لهم، فلحق بأنصارى ومدائنى وأعرابى.
2. . قال محمود: «وهي منصوبة بفعل مضمر
…. الخ» قال أحمد: في إعراب هذه الآية تورط أبو على الفارسي وتحيز إلى فئة الفتنة وطائفة البدعة، فأعرب رهبانية على أنها منصوبة بفعل مضمر يفسره الظاهر، وعلل امتناع العطف فقال: ألا ترى أن الرهبانية لا يستقيم حملها على جَعَلْنا مع وصفها بقوله ابْتَدَعُوها لأن ما يجعله هو تعالى لا يبتدعونه هم، والزمخشري ورد أيضا مورده الذميم، وأسلمه شيطانه الرجيم، فلما أجاز ما منعه أبو على من جعلها معطوفة: أعذر لذلك بتحريف الجعل إلى التوفيق، فرارا مما فر منه أبو على: من اعتقاد أن ذلك مخلوق لله تعالى، وجنوحا إلى الاشراك واعتقاد أن ما يفعلونه هم لا يفعله الله تعالى ولا يخلقه، وكفى بما في هذه الآية دليلا بعد الأدلة القطعية والبراهين العقلية على بطلان ما اعتقداه، فانه ذكر محل الرحمة والرأفة مع العلم بأن محلها القلب، فجعل قوله فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ تأكيدا لخلقه هذه المعاني وتصويرا لمعنى الخلق بذكر محله، ولو كان المراد أمرا غير مخلوق في قلوبهم لله تعالى كما زعما: لم يبق لقوله في قلوب الذين اتبعوه موقع، ويأبى الله أن يشتمل كتابه الكريم على مالا موقع له، ألهمنا الله الحجة وتهج بنا واضح المحجة، إنه ولى التوفيق وواهب التحقيق.
16
Q 57:26 · Vol. 4, p. 481

Verse 26

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And We sent Noah and Abraham, and placed prophethood and the Book among their descendants; some of them are guided, and many of them are defiantly disobedient (26)
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً وَإِبْراهِيمَ وَجَعَلْنا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتابَ فَمِنْهُمْ مُهْتَدٍ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ (26)
Vol. 4, p. 481
. “And the Book” is also revelation. From Ibn ʿAbbās: writing with the pen; it is said kataba kitāban and kitābatan. “Among them”: from the descendants, or from those to whom they were sent, and the mention of sending and of the messengers points to them. This is a detailing of their state, that is: some are guided and some are defiantly disobedient, and the majority are the disobedient.
وَالْكِتابَ والوحى. وعن ابن عباس: الخط بالقلم، يقال: كتب كتابا وكتابة مِنْهُمْ فمن الذرية أو من المرسل إليهم، وقد دل عليهم ذكر الإرسال والمرسلين. وهذا تفصيل لحالهم، أى: فمنهم مهتد ومنهم فاسق، والغلبة للفساق.

Q 57:27 · Vol. 4, pp. 481–482

Verse 27

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Then We followed in their footsteps with Our messengers, and We followed with Jesus son of Mary and gave him the Gospel, and placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy, and monasticism which they innovated — We did not prescribe it for them — only seeking God's approval; but they did not observe it with due observance. So We gave those of them who believed their reward, and many of them are defiantly disobedient (27)
ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِرُسُلِنا وَقَفَّيْنا بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ وَآتَيْناهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ وَجَعَلْنا فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً وَرَحْمَةً وَرَهْبانِيَّةً ابْتَدَعُوها ما كَتَبْناها عَلَيْهِمْ إِلاَّ ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ فَما رَعَوْها حَقَّ رِعايَتِها فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ (27)
Vol. 4, p. 481
. Al-Ḥasan read al-Injīl with fatḥa on the hamza, and its matter is lighter than that of barṭīl and sikkīna for those who report them with fatḥa on the fāʾ, because the word is non-Arabic and the preservation of Arabic patterns is not required in it. It is also read raʾāfa, on the pattern faʿāla, that is: We granted them success in mutual compassion and tenderness among themselves. Similar is the description of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ: “compassionate among themselves.” And “rahbāniyya” is their monasticism in the mountains, fleeing from persecution in religion, devoting themselves sincerely to worship; and that is because the tyrants prevailed over the believers after the death of Jesus, fought them three times, and killed them until only a few were left, so they feared being persecuted in their religion and chose monasticism: its meaning is the act attributed to the rahbān «1», who is the fearful: a faʿlān from rahiba, like khashyān from khashiya. It is also read wa-ruhbāniyya with ḍamma, as if attributed to al-ruhbān, which is the plural of rāhib like rākib and rukbān, and it is accusative by an implied verb «2» which the apparent one explains,
قرأ الحسن: الإنجيل، بفتح الهمزة، وأمره أهون من أمر البرطيل والسكينة فيمن رواهما بفتح الفاء، لأنّ الكلمة أعجمية لا يلزم فيها حفظ أبنية العرب. وقرئ: رآفة، على: فعالة، أى: وفقناهم للتراحم والتعاطف بينهم. ونحوه في صفة أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رُحَماءُ بَيْنَهُمْ. والرهبانية: ترهبهم في الجبال فارّين من الفتنة في الدين، مخلصين أنفسهم للعبادة، وذلك أنّ الجبابرة ظهروا على المؤمنين بعد موت عيسى، فقاتلوهم ثلاث مرات، فقتلوا حتى لم يبق منهم إلا القليل، فخافوا أن يفتنوا في دينهم، فاختاروا الرهبانية: ومعناها الفعلة المنسوبة إلى الرهبان، «1» وهو الخائف: فعلان من رهب، كخشيان من خشي. وقرئ: ورهبانية بالضم، كأنها نسبة إلى الرهبان: وهو جمع راهب كراكب وركبان، وانتصابها بفعل مضمر «2» يفسره
Vol. 4, p. 482
its estimate: “and they innovated monasticism.” “They innovated it,” meaning: they originated it from themselves and vowed it. “We did not prescribe it for them,” We did not make it obligatory upon them; “only seeking God's approval” is a disconnected exception, that is: but they innovated it seeking God's approval; “but they did not observe it with due observance,” as the one who vows must observe his vow, because it is a covenant with God which it is not lawful to break. “So We gave those who believed,” he means: the people of mercy and compassion who followed Jesus; “and many of them are defiantly disobedient,” those who did not keep their vow. It is also possible that rahbāniyya is conjoined to what precedes, and “they innovated it” is a description of it, in the accusative position, that is: We placed in their hearts compassion, mercy and a monasticism innovated by them, meaning: We granted them success in mutual compassion and in innovating monasticism and originating it; “We did not prescribe it for them except that they seek by it God's approval and deserve by it reward,” on the basis that He prescribed it for them and obliged them to it so that they might escape persecutions and seek by that God's pleasure and reward; “but they all did not observe it with due observance, but some of them did; so We gave the believers among them who observed monasticism their reward, and many of them are defiantly disobedient,” and they are those who did not observe it.
الظاهر: تقديره. وابتدعوا رهبانية ابْتَدَعُوها يعنى: وأحدثوها من عند أنفسهم ونذروها ما كَتَبْناها عَلَيْهِمْ لم نفرضها نحن عليهم إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ استثناء منقطع، أى: ولكنهم ابتدعوها ابتغاء رضوان الله فَما رَعَوْها حَقَّ رِعايَتِها كما يجب على الناذر رعاية نذره، لأنه عهد مع الله لا يحل نكثه فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يريد: أهل الرحمة والرأفة الذين اتبعوا عيسى وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ الذين لم يحافظوا على نذرهم. ويجوز أن تكون الرهبانية معطوفة على ما قبلها، وابتدعوها: صفة لها في محل النصب، أى: وجعلنا في قلوبهم رأفة ورحمة ورهبانية مبتدعة من عندهم، بمعنى: وقفناهم للتراحم بينهم ولابتداع الرهبانية واستحداثها، ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ليبتغوا بها رضوان الله ويستحقوا بها الثواب، على أنه كتبها عليهم وألزمها إياهم ليتخلصوا من الفتن ويبتغوا بذلك رضا الله وثوابه، فما رعوها جميعا حق رعايتها، ولكن بعضهم، فآتينا المؤمنين المراعين منهم للرهبانية أجرهم، وكثير منهم فاسقون. وهم الذين لم يرعوها.

Q 57:28 · Vol. 4, p. 482

Verse 28

The verse as the commentary quotes it
O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you walk, and forgive you; and God is Forgiving, Merciful (28)
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ نُوراً تَمْشُونَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (28)
Vol. 4, p. 482
. “O you who believe”: it may be an address to those who believed from the People of the Book and those who believed «1» from others. If it is an address to the believers of the People of the Book, the meaning is: O you who believed in Moses and Jesus, believe in Muḥammad; “He will give you,” God, “a double portion,” that is, two shares, “of His mercy” for your belief in Muḥammad and your belief in those before him; “and make for you,” on the Day of Resurrection, “a light by which you walk,” which is the light mentioned in His saying “their light runs”; “and forgive you” what you advanced of unbelief and sins.
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يجوز أن يكون خطابا للذين آمنوا من أهل الكتاب والذين آمنوا «1» من غيرهم، فإن كان خطابا لمؤمنى أهل الكتاب. فالمعنى: يا أيها الذين آمنوا بموسى وعيسى آمنوا بمحمد يُؤْتِكُمْ الله كِفْلَيْنِ أى نصيبين مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ لإيمانكم بمحمد وإيمانكم بمن قبله وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ يوم القيامة نُوراً تَمْشُونَ بِهِ وهو النور المذكور في قوله يَسْعى نُورُهُمْ. وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ما أسلفتم من الكفر والمعاصي.

Q 57:29 · Vol. 4, pp. 482–484

Verse 29

The verse as the commentary quotes it
So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of God's bounty, and that bounty is in God's hand; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty (29)
لِئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ أَلاَّ يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى شَيْءٍ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَأَنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ (29)
Vol. 4, p. 483
“Li-allā yaʿlama” means li-yaʿlama, “the People of the Book” who did not become Muslim, and lā is redundant; “allā yaqdirūna”: an is lightened from the heavy, its origin being annahu lā yaqdirūna, meaning: the situation is that they have no power “over anything of God's bounty,” that is: they do not obtain anything of what was mentioned of His bounty, namely the two portions, the light and the forgiveness, because they did not believe in the Messenger of God, so their belief in those before him did not benefit them and did not earn them any bounty at all. If it is an address to others, the meaning is: fear God and remain firm in your belief in the Messenger of God; He will give you what He promised to the believers among the People of the Book of the two portions in His saying “those will be given their reward twice,” and will not diminish for you the like of their reward, because you are like them in the two beliefs, not differentiating between any of His messengers. It is reported that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent Jaʿfar ؓ with seventy riders to the Negus to call him; Jaʿfar came to him and called him, and he responded to him, and some people who had believed from among the people of his kingdom, forty men, said: Permit us to go as a delegation to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He permitted them, and they came with Jaʿfar when [the Prophet] had prepared for the battle of Uḥud; when they saw the poverty of the Muslims, they asked leave of the Messenger of God ﷺ and went back and returned with wealth of theirs with which they consoled the Muslims «1». So God sent down “Those to whom We gave the Book … up to … and spend of what We provided them.” When those of the People of the Book who had not believed heard His saying “they will be given their reward twice,” they boasted over the Muslims and said: As for whoever believed in your Book and our Book, he has his reward twice; and as for whoever did not believe in your Book, he has a reward like yours; so what is your excellence over us? Then it was revealed. It is also reported that the believers of the People of the Book boasted over other believers that they are given their reward twice, and claimed excellence over them; so it was revealed. It is also read li-kay yaʿlama, and li-kaylā yaʿlama, and li-yaʿlama, and li-an yaʿlama, with assimilation of the nūn into the yāʾ, and li-yan yaʿlama, with the hamza changed into yāʾ and assimilation of the nūn into the yāʾ. From al-Ḥasan: liyalla yaʿlama, with fatḥa on the lām and sukūn on the yāʾ; Quṭrub reported it with kasra on the lām. It is said about its explanation: the hamza of an was dropped and its nūn assimilated into the lām of lā, so it became lillā, then the assimilated lām was replaced by yāʾ, as they say dīwān and qīrāṭ. And whoever put fatḥa on the lām [did so] because the original of the preposition lām is fatḥa, as he recited: “I want to forget her mention.” «2» ..
لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ ليعلم أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ الذين لم يسلموا، ولا مزيدة أَلَّا يَقْدِرُونَ أن مخففة من الثقيلة، أصله: أنه لا يقدرون، يعنى: أنّ الشأن لا يقدرون عَلى شَيْءٍ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ أى: لا ينالون شيئا مما ذكر من فضله من الكفلين: والنور والمغفرة، لأنهم لم يؤمنوا برسول الله، فلم ينفعهم إيمانهم بمن قبله، ولم يكسبهم فضلا قط. وإن كان خطابا لغيرهم، فالمعنى: اتقوا الله واثبتوا على إيمانكم برسول الله يؤتكم ما وعد من آمن من أهل الكتاب من الكفلين في قوله أُولئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ ولا ينقصكم من مثل أجرهم، لأنكم مثلهم في الإيمانين لا تفرقون بين أحد من رسله. روى أنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث جعفرا رضى الله عنه في سبعين راكبا إلى النجاشي يدعوه، فقدم جعفر عليه فدعاه فاستجاب له، فقال ناس ممن آمن من أهل مملكته وهم أربعون رجلا. ائذن لنا في الوفادة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأذن لهم فقدموا مع جعفر وقد تهيأ لوقعة أحد، فلما رأوا ما بالمسلمين من خصاصة: استأذنوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فرجعوا وقدموا بأموال لهم فآسوا بها المسلمين «1» ، فأنزل الله الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ … إلى قوله … وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ فلما سمع من لم يؤمن من أهل الكتاب قوله يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ فخروا على المسلمين وقالوا: أما من آمن بكتابكم وكتابنا فله أجره مرّتين، وأما من لم يؤمن بكتابكم فله أجر كأجركم، فما فضلكم علينا؟ فنزلت. وروى أنّ مؤمنى أهل الكتاب افتخروا على غيرهم من المؤمنين بأنهم يؤتون أجرهم مرّتين، وادعوا الفضل عليهم، فنزلت. وقرئ لكي يعلم. ولكيلا يعلم. وليعلم. ولأن يعلم: بإدغام النون في الياء. ولين يعلم: بقلب الهمزة ياء وإدغام النون في الياء. وعن الحسن: ليلا يعلم، بفتح اللام وسكون الياء. ورواه قطرب بكسر اللام. وقيل في وجهها: حذفت همزة أن، وأدغمت نونها في لام لا، فصار «للا» ثم أبدلت من اللام المدغمة ياء، كقولهم: ديوان، وقيراط. ومن فتح اللام فعلى أن أصل لام الجرّ الفتح، كما أنشد: أريد لأنسى ذكرها. «2» ..
Vol. 4, p. 484
It is also read an lā yaqdirū. “In God's hand” means in His dominion and disposal; and the “hand” is a figure. “He gives it to whom He wills,” and He wills only to give it to one who deserves it. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Whoever recites Sūrat al-Ḥadīd will be written among those who believe in God and His messengers” «1».
وقرئ: أن لا يقدروا بِيَدِ اللَّهِ في ملكه وتصرفه. واليد مثل يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ ولا يشاء إلا إيتاء من يستحقه. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة الحديد كتب من الذين آمنوا بالله ورسله» «1» .

1. (1) . It is well known that Jaʿfar only came some time after Uḥud, at the conquest of Khaybar. [.....]
2. . “I want to forget her mention, yet it is as if … Laylā appears to me on every path.” By Qays b. al-Mulawwaḥ, the Majnūn of Laylā al-ʿĀmiriyya. It is also said: by Kuthayyir, the companion of ʿAzza, and he alluded to her by Laylā as a cover. It is also said that Kuthayyir stole it from the poetry of Jamīl, the companion of Buthayna. His saying “li-ansā,” with fatḥa on the preposition lām, is according to the original for single-letter particles, and that is the language of ʿUkl, and it is necessary in it when it enters a verb made accusative by an implied an, as here. It is also narrated with kasra, according to the well-known dialect, that is: “I want, for the forgetting of her mention,” with the lām redundant, but it is what signaled the omission of “an.” And tamaththala: its origin is tatamaththala, that is, takes shape and appears before me, Laylā, by every road, either the sensory road or the road of remembrance, and the first is more probable, by the evidence of his saying “as if”; and her appearing to him necessitates his remembering her. And mā is redundant after ka-anna, restraining it from acting, which is why it entered the verb.
1. (1) . المعروف أن جعفر إنما قدم بعد أحد بزمان، قدم عند فتح خيبر. [.....]
2. . أريد لأنسى ذكرها فكأنما
…. تمثل لي ليلى بكل سبيل لقبس بن الملوح مجنون ليلى العامرية. وقيل: لكثير صاحب عزة، وكنى عنها بليلى تسترا. وقيل: سرقه كثير من شعر جميل صاحب بثنية. وقوله: لأنسى بفتح لام الجر على الأصل في الحروف المفردة، وتلك: لغة عكل، ويتعين فيها إذا دخلت على فعل منصوب بأن مضمرة كما هنا. وتروى بالكسر على اللغة المشهورة، أى: أريد لنسيان تذكرها، واللام زائدة، لكنها هي التي أشعرت بحذف «إن» ، وتمثل: أصله تتمثل، أى تتشكل وتتخيل أمامى ليلى بكل طريق، إما الحسى وإما طريق الذكر، والأول أوجه، بدليل قوله «كأنما» وتمثلها له يوجب تذكرها. وما زائدة بعد كان، كافة لها عن العمل فلذلك دخلت على الفعل.
Vol. 4, p. 484
1. (1) . Al-Thaʿlabī, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wāḥidī reported it with their chains to Ubayy [b.] Kaʿb.
2. . Maḥmūd said: “ʿĀʾisha ؓ said: Praise be to God who encompassed in His hearing all voices … etc.” Aḥmad said: Some have used it as evidence for the non-obligation of ẓihār on the dhimmī, but that is not strong, because it is not what is intended.
3. . Reported by al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, al-Ṭabarī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq and al-Bazzār by way of al-Aʿmash from Tamīm b. Salama from ʿUrwa from ʿĀʾisha. Al-Bukhārī gave it in suspended form, and al-Ḥākim reported it in fuller wording, in which she and her husband are named.
4. . His statement «wa-lamam»: that is, a touch of madness, or a touch from the jinn. Stated in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿ)
5. . Reported by al-Dāraquṭnī and al-Bayhaqī.

3. . أخرجه النسائي وابن ماجة والطبري وأحمد وإسحاق والبزار من طريق الأعمش عن تميم بن سلمة عن عروة عن عائشة. وعلقه البخاري، وأخرجه الحاكم أتم سياقا منه، وفيه تسميتها وتسمية زوجها.
